newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: U.S. Trade Representative asks APEC to back ITA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Trade Representative asks APEC to back ITA.

text.p: The United States called on APEC on Friday to put its money where its mouth is and back an Information Technology Agreement (ITA) to free global trade in computers and parts estimated to be worth $1.8 trillion.
Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said information technology was absolutely essential to world development and needed free and open competition to develop.

Barshefsky told a conference of business leaders coinciding with the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum conference that information technology products were the infrastructure of the 21st Century.
"They are and will be to that century what roads and bridges were to the 19th Century," she said.
Leaders of APEC's 18 member economies are due to hold their fourth annual summit on Monday in Subic Bay, near Manila.
"We must keep pace with the infrastructure requirements of the 21st Century and we must in that sense put our money where our mouth is," Barshefsky said.
"We have proposed that APEC endorse the efforts that are now going on at the WTO to complete an information technology agreement by the Singapore ministerial (meeting)."
The World Trade Organisation (WTO) will hold its first ministerial meeting in Singapore in December.
Barshefsky said the information technology industry was growing and developing so rapidly that APEC members could not afford to apply tariffs or what she called "taxes" on it.
"It is the APEC countries that stand to gain most if we reduce taxes on information technology by reducing tariffs."
